subject.title: [Bug]: Scheduled isolated agentTurn outer run records error although session ended success

question: For scheduled isolated agentTurn runs where execution succeeds but post-run delivery/finalization fails, should OpenClaw record primary cron status as `ok` with delivery fields, introduce a first-class `warning` status, or keep some delivery failures as primary `error`?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes persisted cron status, operator alerts, and retry/backoff behavior, so automation should not choose the public status contract on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept narrow status split
options.body: Use `status=ok` for successful isolated execution and surface post-run send failures through `deliveryStatus`, `deliveryError`, diagnostics, and run-log fields.

options.title: Use first-class warning
options.body: Defer the narrow fix and land a broader `warning` status contract across storage, Gateway schema, CLI/UI, docs, and plugin/API consumers.

options.title: Keep delivery failures as errors
options.body: Preserve current primary-error behavior for delivery failures and instead improve diagnostics so users can distinguish execution failure from delivery failure.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow status split
recommendation.body: Use `status=ok` for successful isolated execution and surface post-run send failures through `deliveryStatus`, `deliveryError`, diagnostics, and run-log fields.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the cron finalizer and delivery/status boundary involved in this product contract.
